html:
The Kaskaskia were one of the main peoples of the Illinois Confederation, Algonquian-speaking tribes of the prairies along the Illinois and Mississippi rivers. Their first recorded meeting with Europeans was at a Jesuit mission near Green Bay in 1667.

From the 1670s they lived at the Grand Village of the Illinois near Starved Rock, a town of thousands where the French set up a mission. Around 1703 they moved south to the Mississippi, where they and the French founded the village of Kaskaskia, which later served as the first capital of the state of Illinois. War, alcohol and disease cut their numbers. In 1803 they gave up most of their land to the United States, and later they joined the Peoria in Kansas and Oklahoma. See also New France.
